title: The Bride of Christ
subtitle: Israel, the Church, and the One Bride of Revelation 19
question: “The Bride of Christ” is one of the most familiar expressions in Christian teaching, but familiarity with a theological expression does not by itself establish how Scripture assigns that identity.

title: The Gospel of the Kingdom
subtitle: Israel, the Kingdom Message, and the Promises of God
question: The phrase “the gospel of the kingdom” is often treated as a general synonym for the message of salvation, but Scripture places it within a specific prophetic setting already known to Israel.

title: The Body of Christ and the Tribulation
subtitle: Does God’s Prophetic Program Include the Church?
question: The Tribulation question is often approached first as a question of timing: before, during, or after. This study begins one step earlier by asking whom Scripture identifies with the coming prophetic period and to which revealed program it belongs.

title: Israel and the Body of Christ
subtitle: Seven Distinctions That Clarify God’s Revealed Purposes
question: Few doctrinal distinctions affect biblical interpretation more profoundly than the distinction between Israel and the Church, the Body of Christ. title: The Heavenly Calling
subtitle: The Body of Christ’s Position, Hope, and Purpose in the Heavenly Places
question: Paul’s teaching presents a coherent, Christ-centered calling—not simply the expectation of going to heaven. title: The Mystery Revealed Through Paul
subtitle: Understanding God’s Previously Hidden Purpose for the Body of Christ
question: In Scripture, Mystery refers to truth deliberately kept hidden in God’s redemptive plan until revealed through Paul. It is not obscurity—it is timing. title: The Day of the Lord
subtitle: Israel’s Prophetic Day and the Body of Christ’s Heavenly Hope
question: The Day of the Lord is first established in the prophets. Its repeated vocabulary marks an extended period of divine intervention characterized by wrath, darkness, judgment, and the visible return of Christ, culminating in Israel’s restoration.

title: The Day of Christ
subtitle: The Body of Christ’s Heavenly Hope, Gathering, and Glorification
question: The Day of Christ belongs exclusively to the Body’s heavenly hope and is defined first by Paul’s own language. title: The Remnant
subtitle: God’s Faithfulness to Israel Through Judgment, Preservation, and Promise
question: The remnant is not a new people replacing Israel. A remnant of Israel remains Israel. In Elijah’s day, in Paul’s day, and in Israel’s prophetic future, preservation confirms that God has not cast away His people.

title: Daniel’s Seventieth Week
subtitle: Israel’s Final Prophetic Week, the Great Tribulation, and the Coming Kingdom
question: Daniel 9 gives Scripture’s controlling prophetic structure for Israel and Jerusalem. Its remaining seventieth week is not exhausted by the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70, nor is it transferred to the Body of Christ. The prophecy awaits its future fulfillment within Israel’s Prophecy Program.

title: The Beginning of the Body of Christ
subtitle: Why the Church Which Is Christ’s Body Begins with Paul at Acts 9
question: The Church, which is Christ’s Body, belongs to the previously hidden Mystery revealed through Paul. Because the Body is part of that Mystery Program, it cannot be placed historically within Israel’s Prophecy Program before the Mystery begins with Paul in Acts 9.

title: The New Covenant
subtitle: Israel’s Promised Restoration Under Messiah
question: Jeremiah 31 identifies Israel and Judah as the New Covenant’s named parties. Ezekiel 36 complements that promise with cleansing, a new heart, the Spirit within restored Israel, regathering, and restoration to the land. The covenant arrangement is new; the named covenant people are not.

title: The Olive Tree and the Body of Christ
subtitle: Participation, Identity, and the Acts Overlap
question: Paul begins Romans 11 by denying that God has cast away His people Israel. Israel remains the natural-branch nation even amid unbelief, stumbling, partial blindness, and broken branches. The patriarchal root remains the source of prophetic blessing and privilege; Gentiles are a wild branch grafted i

title: Acts 9 and the Beginning of Mystery
subtitle: Paul’s Calling, Distinct Apostleships, and the Acts Overlap
question: Acts 9 must be read against the setting Luke has already established: Israel, Jerusalem, the Twelve, Kingdom testimony, prophetic promise, and signs are all operative before Saul is called. Paul’s apostleship is not an extension of the Twelve’s Kingdom Commission; it begins with the risen Christ’s i

title: Faith and Works in James and Paul
subtitle: Two Apostolic Settings, Distinct Audiences and Requirements
question: James addresses an Israel-oriented, covenantal audience and insists that a professed faith which remains barren is dead. His conclusion—that a person is justified by works and not by faith only—must be read within that stated setting.

title: The Believer's Identity in Christ
subtitle: Union, Standing, Security, and the Heavenly Calling of the Body
question: Paul repeatedly locates the believer’s standing “in Christ.” That expression directs attention away from self-construction and toward divine accomplishment. The believer is identified with Christ, made part of one Body under Him as Head, accepted and complete in Him, and sealed by the Spirit.

title: The Abrahamic Covenant
subtitle: Promise, Covenant Line, Land, and Blessing in Israel's Prophetic Purpose
question: Genesis does not leave the covenant’s shape undefined. Its promises concern Abraham’s covenant line, the nation that comes through that line, a defined land promise, and blessing that reaches outward to the nations. The particularity of the covenant line does not deny Gentile blessing; it explains t

title: Peter and Paul: Distinct Apostolic Commissions
subtitle: Same Lord, Distinct Apostleships During the Acts Overlap
question: Shared faith in Christ and common service to Him do not require identical commissions. Peter’s apostleship is rooted in the Twelve, Israel, and the promised Kingdom. Paul’s apostleship is not derived from Peter or the Twelve, but from the risen Lord’s direct calling and revelation.

title: The Jerusalem Council
subtitle: Fellowship and Distinction During the Acts Overlap
question: Acts 15 did not create Paul’s Gentile ministry or make Jerusalem the source of his apostleship. The council faced a concrete controversy: whether Gentile believers had to be circumcised and placed under Israel’s Mosaic administration in order to stand properly before God.

title: Understanding Acts 2:38
subtitle: Peter’s Pentecostal Call to Israel in Its Prophetic Setting
question: Acts 2:38 is not a detached salvation formula but Peter’s direct answer to Israelites who have just heard his prophetic explanation of Pentecost, his announcement of the risen Messiah, and his indictment of Israel’s rejection of Him.

title: Israel’s Judicial Blinding
subtitle: Hardening, Purpose, and the Hope of Restoration
question: Judicial blinding is a real national judgment, but it is neither individually exhaustive nor covenant-canceling. Believing Israelites remain, Israel’s promises remain valid, and Romans 11 looks ahead to future restoration.

title: Prayer Under Grace
subtitle: Understanding Prayer in the Believer’s Grace Standing, Not Covenant Obligation
question: Prayer did not begin with the Mystery, and it is not diminished under Grace. Scripture records prayer throughout its history, yet a recurring practice does not make every promise attached to prayer identical for every audience.

title: The 144,000
subtitle: Israel’s Sealed Servants in God’s Prophetic Program
question: The 144,000 are neither the entirety of Israel’s believing remnant nor a symbolic title for the Body of Christ. Revelation identifies them as a specific, numbered, sealed company from Israel’s tribes.

title: The Willful Sin Warning
subtitle: Understanding Hebrews 10:26–31 in Its Covenant and Prophetic Context
question: The warning in Hebrews 10 is not a detached statement about ordinary moral failure. Its language concerns a decisive rejection of the Son, His covenant blood, and the Spirit of grace after receiving the knowledge of the truth.

title: The Signs That Followed
subtitle: Understanding Mark 16:16–18 in Israel’s Kingdom and Prophetic Program
question: The signs in Mark 16 are not a spectacle or a checklist for every individual believer. Mark 16:20 identifies their purpose: the Lord confirmed the word preached by His commissioned messengers.

title: The Seven Churches of Revelation
subtitle: Historical Assemblies, Their Prophetic Setting, and the Messages of Christ
question: The word church identifies an assembly, but it does not by itself establish that assembly as the Church which is Christ’s Body. Audience, message, promise, setting, and revealed purpose must determine programmatic identity.

title: Israel’s Seven Appointed Feasts
subtitle: Their Covenant Setting, Historical Observance, and Prophetic Significance
question: The LORD appointed the feasts to Israel, joining sacred time to national history, the land, harvest, priestly service, remembrance, cleansing, and rejoicing.

title: The Warning of Hebrews 6:4–6
subtitle: Enlightened, Tasting the Heavenly Gift, Falling Away, and the Impossibility of Renewal
question: The warning does not stand alone. It grows from the rebuke for dullness of hearing, the call to move beyond foundational instruction, and the book’s wider pattern of privilege, accountability, endurance, and promised inheritance.

title: One Taken and the Other Left
subtitle: Matthew 24:40–41 and Luke 17:34–36 in the Context of Christ’s Second Coming
question: Popular teaching often treats “taken” as automatic deliverance and “left” as abandonment. Jesus’ own comparisons reverse that assumption: the Flood overtook the unprepared, Lot’s world was destroyed, and a preserved company remained alive through judgment.

title: Seated With Christ in Heavenly Places
subtitle: The Meaning, Boundaries, and Future Implications of the Body’s Position in Christ
question: Ephesians first presents Christ raised and seated far above every principality, power, might, dominion, and name. It then presents believers as made alive, raised, and seated together in Him. Christ’s exaltation is primary; the Body’s position is derivative, relational, and wholly grounded in grace.

title: The Judgments of Scripture
subtitle: Their Subjects, Timing, Standards, Purposes, and Outcomes
question: The Judge is always righteous, but Scripture assigns different judgments to different subjects, times, standards, purposes, and outcomes. title: Covenant Theology and Dispensational Theology
subtitle: Comparing the Major Systems That Organize Biblical Revelation
question: A framework determines how readers connect earlier promises with later revelation, classify continuity and distinction, identify the recipients of covenants, and understand Israel, the Church, prophecy, and the Kingdom. Those assumptions shape conclusions even when the reader does not use a formal t

title: The Crowns of Scripture
subtitle: Distinguishing Their Recipients, Timing, Basis, and Purpose
question: Scripture uses crowns for disciplined service, ministry fruit, faithful completion, endurance, shepherding, overcoming, delegated authority, worship, symbolic identity, and Christ’s royal supremacy. Similar imagery does not make every passage identical in audience or purpose.

title: Filled Again
subtitle: Why the Holy Spirit Empowered God’s Servants Multiple Times in Acts
question: Acts 2 and Acts 4 give the clearest evidence: the same prophetic company is filled more than once, first at Pentecost and later in answer to prayer for boldness. title: Who Is the Israel of God?
subtitle: Spiritual Israel, the Jew Inwardly, and the Boundaries of Biblical Identity
question: Paul recognizes Israel, Gentiles, and the Body of Christ without making those categories interchangeable. Faith and inward spiritual reality matter profoundly, but neither ethnic descent alone nor participation in grace settles the corporate identity question.

title: Jews, Gentiles, and the Church of God
subtitle: The Threefold Identity of 1 Corinthians 10:32
question: Paul’s command works because Jews, Gentiles, and the Church of God are recognizable categories. Yet the verse is not a simplistic census of mutually exclusive social identities. title: What Does Paul Mean by “New Creation”?
subtitle: Individual Renewal, Corporate Identity, and the Boundaries of Pauline Doctrine
question: Paul’s language announces a divine act accomplished in Christ. It describes a real standing and corporate order established by God, not merely a believer’s improved habits, changing emotions, or gradual moral development.

title: Why Acts Is Not a Universal Experience Manual
subtitle: Narrative Events, Apostolic Authority, and Present Governing Doctrine
question: Luke’s accounts are inspired and instructive, but their authority must be read according to what they say. Acts includes Israel’s continuing prophetic ministry and the Mystery revealed through Paul, with both present from Acts 9 through Acts 28.

title: The Church’s Relationship to Israel’s Scriptures
subtitle: How the Body Reads, Learns from, and Applies the Old Testament Without Identity Transfer
question: The Church should read Israel’s Scriptures closely. They reveal God’s character and works, testify to Christ, expose sin, and supply hope and warning. Their value is clearest when the reader preserves what God said, to whom He said it, and in what setting.

title: Who IsAbraham’s Seed?
subtitle: Faith, Promise, Inheritance, and the Difference Between Blessing and Israelite Identity
question: Abraham’s seed can describe natural descendants, the selected covenant line, Christ, or people who belong to Christ. Treating every occurrence as though it names the same group turns Paul’s precise claims into a sweeping identity claim he does not make.

title: Kingdom of God orKingdom of Heaven?

question: Where Matthew, Mark, and Luke report the same sayings, “kingdom of heaven” and “kingdom of God” name the same kingdom—Matthew 19:23–24 uses both for one entrance into one kingdom. title: One Baptism
subtitle: Water Baptism, Spirit Baptism, and the Body of Christ
question: Baptism in Scripture means identification, and the element varies: water, the Spirit, suffering, even a cloud and a sea. Reading each baptism by its agent, element, and result removes most of the contradictions readers find when every use of the word is assumed to mean the same act.

title: The Gospel of the Grace of God
subtitle: Paul’s Gospel: Its Content, Its Audience, and the Faith It Calls For
question: Paul spoke of his gospel with exact language: its names, its content, its audience, and the response it calls for. Reading those distinctions in order removes the vagueness that lets “gospel” mean whatever a reader assumes.

subtitle: The Believer's Daily Walk, the Flesh, and the Fruit of the Spirit
